title: UAE’s oil potential boosted by promising shale discovery | Wood Mackenize
gist: EOG Resources' first two wells in the UAE's Shilaif shale formation each produced over 25,000 barrels of oil in their first 30 days from one-mile laterals, outperforming on a per-foot basis some of the best US tight oil acreage; ADNOC pegs the formation's technically recoverable resource at up to 22 billion barrels, and the UAE is backing a $145 billion decade-long upstream investment push while having exited OPEC in 2026.

insights.claim: ADNOC has identified up to 22 billion barrels of technically recoverable unconventional oil in the Upper Cretaceous Shilaif Formation in the UAE.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: A resource base of this size positions Shilaif as a potential new-tier global shale play worth tracking for upstream investment and future UAE export capacity.
insights.quote: ADNOC announced the discovery of up to 22 billion barrels of technically recoverable unconventional oil in the Upper Cretaceous Shilaif Formation several years ago.
insights.locator: Why did you rate Shilaif so highly?

insights.claim: Unlike other unconventional projects in the UAE region, the Shilaif Formation is primarily an oil-prone (not gas-prone) reservoir with encouraging reservoir properties.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Oil-prone economics generally command better netbacks than gas-prone unconventional plays, supporting the investment case for Shilaif over regional peers.
insights.locator: Why did you rate Shilaif so highly?

insights.claim: Shilaif is understood to be geologically analogous to the liquids-prone area of the Eagle Ford play in Texas, where EOG Resources is already a major producer.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: EOG's existing Eagle Ford operating playbook and technical experience can likely transfer to Shilaif, de-risking execution relative to a wholly novel play.
insights.quote: Shilaif is understood to be analogous with the liquids-prone area of the Eagle Ford play in Texas where EOG Resources is a major producer.
insights.locator: How did the exploration drilling go?

insights.claim: EOG Resources' first two Shilaif wells, each drilled with one-mile laterals and brought online in June 2026, produced more than 25,000 barrels of oil each in their first 30 days and are currently flowing naturally before transitioning to artificial lift.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: This is a concrete, verifiable early productivity benchmark investors can compare against subsequent Shilaif wells to gauge whether the play is scaling as hoped.
insights.quote: The two wells, each with one-mile laterals, drilled and brought online in June, each produced more than 25,000 barrels of oil in their first 30 days and are currently flowing naturally before transitioning to artificial lift.
insights.locator: How did the exploration drilling go?

insights.claim: On a per-foot basis, EOG's initial Shilaif wells outperform because they achieved 25,000-barrel 30-day cumulative production from one-mile laterals, half the length of typical two-mile-plus laterals used in the US Permian and Eagle Ford, indicating unusually strong reservoir quality.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Superior per-foot productivity suggests Shilaif could become cost-competitive with, or superior to, leading US shale plays once lateral lengths are extended, a key driver of future capital allocation to the play.
insights.quote: On a per-foot basis, EOG’s UAE wells clearly outperform indicating promising reservoir quality.
insights.locator: What’s so good about the results?

insights.claim: The first two Shilaif wells were located in the same area and landing zone, so repeatability of these strong results across EOG's broader UC03 acreage remains unproven.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Investors should treat the early results as a promising but narrow data point, not yet evidence of play-wide commerciality; watch for well results outside the initial landing zone.
insights.quote: The first two wells were located in the same area and landing zone, meaning repeatability across the broader EOG acreage is still unproven.
insights.locator: Doesn’t Shilaif still have it all to prove after only two wells?

insights.claim: EOG Resources was granted the UAE's first unconventional exploration licence, UC03, covering 900,000 acres, in May 2025.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: This establishes a concrete acreage position and timeline for EOG's UAE shale entry that investors can use to benchmark pace of development against other international shale ventures.
insights.quote: EOG Resources, a leading US-based shale explorer with international experience and a track record of finding new unconventional plays, was granted its first licence - UC03 covering 900,000-acres, in May 2025.
insights.locator: Why did you rate Shilaif so highly?

insights.claim: The UAE has differentiated itself from other regional governments by awarding shale concessions to foreign E&P companies, with ADNOC and its subsidiaries actively supporting participation by international service companies and labour.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: A foreign-investor-friendly licensing regime lowers the barrier for other international operators to enter UAE unconventional plays, potentially accelerating capital inflows to the sector.
insights.quote: The UAE has taken a different approach to other governments in the region by awarding concessions to foreign E&P companies.
insights.locator: Why did you rate Shilaif so highly?

insights.claim: The UC03 licence is structured as a concession with tax and royalty terms rather than a production sharing contract, a structure considered better suited to the sustained, long-cycle investment typical of unconventional projects.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Fiscal terms shape investment economics directly; a concession-style regime is a structural positive for continued foreign shale capital commitment in the UAE versus PSC-based peers.
insights.quote: UCO3 is structured as a concession with tax and royalty terms rather than a production sharing contract. Concessions are better suited to the sustained investment typical of unconventional projects.
insights.locator: What’s so good about the results?

insights.claim: EOG Resources has a track record of moving quickly to test new international unconventional plays, having entered Oman in 2020, Indonesia in 2024, and Bahrain in 2025 prior to the UAE.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: EOG's repeatable fast-entry international shale strategy suggests the Shilaif move is part of a broader, proven exploration playbook rather than a one-off bet.
insights.quote: EOG has a track record of moving quickly to test new international plays, moving at a similar pace in Oman (2020), Indonesia (2024) and Bahrain (2025).
insights.locator: Why did you rate Shilaif so highly?

insights.claim: The initial Shilaif wells were drilled and completed using only locally available drilling and completion services, leaving meaningful room for cost reduction if higher-spec equipment, longer laterals, and further optimisation are deployed once commerciality is confirmed.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Unit-cost improvement potential from equipment upgrades and longer laterals is a lever investors should watch as evidence the play's breakeven economics could improve materially over time.
insights.quote: EOG has indicated that these wells were drilled with locally available drilling and completion services.
insights.locator: What’s so good about the results?

insights.claim: Besides EOG, PETRONAS and a consortium of Bharat Petroleum and Indian Oil are currently drilling wells on blocks near the Shilaif acreage, which will add to industry understanding of the play.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Multiple independent operators drilling nearby blocks will generate additional data points to validate (or undercut) the Shilaif thesis faster than EOG's results alone.
insights.quote: Elsewhere, PETRONAS, and a consortium of Bharat Petroleum and Indian Oil are currently drilling wells on nearby blocks which will add to the understanding.
insights.locator: Doesn’t Shilaif still have it all to prove after only two wells?

insights.claim: Confirming Shilaif's ultimate resource quality and commerciality will require many more wells to establish confidence in long-term decline rates, optimal well spacing, and reservoir variability across the play.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Investors should temper near-term enthusiasm: full commercial validation is a multi-year, multi-well process, not something confirmed by two initial wells.
insights.quote: Ultimately, long-term decline rates, well spacing and reservoir variability will determine the resource quality and commerciality of the play.
insights.locator: Doesn’t Shilaif still have it all to prove after only two wells?

insights.claim: The early Shilaif results suggest the UAE has the potential to join Vaca Muerta in Argentina and Jafurah in Saudi Arabia as one of the only shale plays outside North America to achieve production at scale.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: If validated, Shilaif would join a very short list of internationally scaled shale plays, materially expanding the global unconventional oil supply base investors track outside the US.
insights.quote: Nevertheless, the early results suggest the UAE has the potential to join Vaca Muerta (Argentina) and Jafurah (Saudi Arabia) as the only shale plays outside North America to achieve scale.
insights.locator: Doesn’t Shilaif still have it all to prove after only two wells?

themes.theme: UAE production strategy and OPEC exit

insights.claim: The UAE has committed to investing US$145 billion (real, 2026 terms) in its domestic upstream oil sector over the ten years to 2030.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: This is a large, quantified capex commitment investors can use to size the scale of UAE upstream opportunity and track annual spend against the stated ten-year budget.
insights.quote: The country has committed to investing US$145 billion (real, 2026) in its domestic upstream oil sector over 10 years to 2030.
insights.locator: What does it mean for UAE’s future production?

insights.claim: The UAE's investment programme targets expanding oil production capacity from under 4 million barrels per day in 2020 to 5 million barrels per day by 2027, and ADNOC reported capacity had already reached 4.85 million barrels per day in 2024.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: The UAE is already close to its 5 million b/d 2027 target ahead of schedule, making the target and any beat via Shilaif a near-term, trackable production catalyst.
insights.quote: The overarching goals are to sustain UAE’s oil production and to expand capacity from under 4 million b/d in 2020 to 5 million b/d by 2027. According to ADNOC, capacity reached 4.85 million b/d in 2024.
insights.locator: What does it mean for UAE’s future production?

insights.claim: If Shilaif delivers on the promise shown by its early wells, it increases the chances the UAE stretches its oil production capacity beyond the 5 million barrel-per-day target.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: A capacity overshoot beyond 5 million b/d would be a supply-side upside surprise for global oil markets that investors should monitor as Shilaif appraisal progresses.
insights.quote: Shilaif, if it delivers on the promise of these early wells, increases the chances of stretching capacity beyond the 5 million b/d target.
insights.locator: What does it mean for UAE’s future production?

insights.claim: The UAE left OPEC in 2026 and therefore no longer faces group-imposed constraints on its oil production levels.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Freed from OPEC quota discipline, the UAE can pursue unconstrained production growth from assets like Shilaif, a structural shift relevant to global supply and OPEC+ cohesion analysis.
insights.quote: UAE of course left OPEC in 2026 and no longer has constraints on production levels.
insights.locator: What does it mean for UAE’s future production?

insights.claim: The UAE is planning to expand its oil export pipeline capacity to reduce dependency on the Strait of Hormuz, which would help de-risk future commercialisation of Shilaif output.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Pipeline expansion away from the Hormuz chokepoint reduces geopolitical/shipping risk to UAE export volumes, a relevant factor for insuring or pricing UAE-linked crude supply risk.
insights.quote: Plans to expand oil export pipelines to reduce dependency on the Strait of Hormuz would help derisk future commercialisation of Shilaif.
insights.locator: What does it mean for UAE’s future production?
